sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: The supreme legislative body of the Republic of India, consisting of the **President**, **Rajya Sabha**, and **Lok Sabha**.
Defined under **Part V** (Articles **79 to 122**) of the Constitution of India.
Constituted on **17 April 1952** (first session of Parliament commenced).
New Parliament House, **New Delhi** (Central Vista Redevelopment Project).
**Lok Sabha Speaker**, **Rajya Sabha Chairman** (Vice President of India), Prime Minister, and Members of Parliament (MPs).
Core topic under **General Awareness** and **Indian Polity** scoring high-yield questions on seat numbers, articles, and bill types.
Two houses: **Upper House (Rajya Sabha)** representing states and **Lower House (Lok Sabha)** representing people.
An **integral part** of the Parliament; no bill can become an Act without the President's assent under **Article 111**.

items.title: Parliamentary Articles Structure
items.content:
• **Article 79:** Constitution of Parliament (President + Rajya Sabha + Lok Sabha)
• **Article 80:** Composition of Rajya Sabha (Maximum **250** members)
• **Article 81:** Composition of Lok Sabha (Maximum **550** members)
• **Mnemonic:** **SER**ial numbers: **S** for Sansad (**Art 79**), **E** for Rajya Sabha (**Art 80**), **R** for Lok Sabha (**Art 81**).

items.title: Lok Sabha (House of the People)
items.content:
• Also known as the **First Chamber**, **Popular House**, or **Lower House**.
• Maximum strength: **550** members (**530** from States + **20** from Union Territories).
• Current strength: **543** elected members.
• Normal term: **5 years**, can be dissolved earlier by the President.
• Minimum age for membership: **25 years**.

items.title: Rajya Sabha (Council of States)
items.content:
• Also known as the **Upper House** or **House of Elders**.
• Maximum strength: **250** members (**238** elected from States/UTs + **12** nominated by President for art, literature, science, social service).
• Current strength: **245** members.
• Nature: **Permanent body**, not subject to dissolution; **1/3rd** members retire every **2 years**.
• Minimum age for membership: **30 years**.

items.title: Legislative Procedure & Bill Types
items.content:
• **Ordinary Bill:** Introduced in either House; requires simple majority in both.
• **Money Bill:** Introduced **only in Lok Sabha** on the recommendation of the President (**Article 110**).
• **Financial Bill (I & II):** Deal with revenue/expenditure; **Article 117**.
• **Constitutional Amendment Bill:** Introduced in either House; requires **Special Majority** (**Article 368**).
• **Mnemonic for Bill Types:** **OMCF** -> **O**rdinary, **M**oney, **C**onstitutional Amendment, **F**inancial.

items.title: Key Parliamentary Sessions and Terms
items.content:
• **Budget Session:** February to May (Longest session).
• **Monsoon Session:** July to August.
• **Winter Session:** November to December (Shortest session).
• **Quorum:** **1/10th** of the total members in each house to transact business (**Article 100**).
• **Joint Sitting:** Summoned by the President under **Article 108**, presided over by the **Lok Sabha Speaker**.

items.definition: Remember **S R L** for Articles **79, 80, 81** -> **S**ansad (Art 79), **R**ajya Sabha (Art 80), **L**ok Sabha (Art 81).
Remember **L**ok Sabha comes first alphabetically and requires **25** years; **R**ajya Sabha comes later and requires **30** years.
Remember **M**oney Bill starts with **M**, and **M**aximum power lies with **M**other house (Lok Sabha).
Remember **L**ok Sabha Speaker presides over joint sittings because **L**ok Sabha has more members (**543** vs **245**).
Remember **B**udget, **M**onsoon, **W**inter sessions using car brand **BMW**.
Remember **1/3rd** members retire every **2 years**, ensuring continuity of the Upper House.

items.term: Mistake 1: President is not part of Parliament
items.definition: Students often think Parliament only means Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha. **Correct fact:** The President is an **essential part** of Parliament under Article 79.

items.term: Mistake 2: Money Bill introduction in Rajya Sabha
items.definition: Students confuse Ordinary Bills with Money Bills. **Correct fact:** A Money Bill can **only** be introduced in the Lok Sabha with prior recommendation of the President.
Students think Rajya Sabha dissolves every 5 years like Lok Sabha. **Correct fact:** Rajya Sabha is a **permanent house** and **never dissolves**.

items.term: Mistake 4: Presiding officer of Joint Sitting
items.definition: Students often think the Vice President/Chairman of Rajya Sabha presides over a Joint Sitting. **Correct fact:** The **Lok Sabha Speaker** presides over joint sittings.
Students still believe 2 Anglo-Indians are nominated to Lok Sabha. **Correct fact:** The nomination of Anglo-Indian members was **abolished** by the **104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019**.
Students confuse quorum with majority. **Correct fact:** Quorum is strictly **1/10th** of total members in each house.
Establishes that the Parliament of India consists of the **President**, **Council of States (Rajya Sabha)**, and **House of the People (Lok Sabha)**.
Maximum capacity is **550** members; current elected strength is **543** members representing states and union territories.
Maximum capacity is **250** members, including **12** members nominated by the President for specialized expertise.
Lok Sabha has a normal term of **5 years**, whereas Rajya Sabha is a **permanent body** with members serving **6-year terms**.
Minimum age is **25 years** for Lok Sabha membership and **30 years** for Rajya Sabha membership.
Governed by **Article 110**; Rajya Sabha has restricted powers and must return a Money Bill within **14 days**.
Invoked under **Article 108** by the President to resolve legislative deadlocks between both houses.
Presented annually by the Finance Minister under **Article 112** (Annual Financial Statement).
Elected members of both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha (along with State Legislative Assemblies) participate in electing the President.
Proclamations of National Emergency must be approved by both houses of Parliament within specified statutory timelines.

upscNotes.content: For UPSSSC PET, thoroughly memorize Article numbers (79, 80, 81, 108, 110) and seat counts for Uttar Pradesh in Lok Sabha (80 seats) and Rajya Sabha (31 seats).
UPSSSC often asks questions testing whether Rajya Sabha can vote on Demands for Grants. Remember: Demands for Grants are voted **only in the Lok Sabha**, not in the Rajya Sabha.
Pay close attention to recent current affairs regarding Parliament, such as the inauguration of the new Parliament building under the Central Vista project.
Do not confuse the Chairperson of Rajya Sabha with its elected members. The Vice President is the **ex-officio** Chairman and is **not** a member of the Rajya Sabha.

keyTakeaways: Indian Parliament is bicameral, comprising the President, Lok Sabha, and Rajya Sabha under Part V (Articles 79-122).
Lok Sabha is the Lower House with 543 current members, requiring a minimum age of 25 years.
Rajya Sabha is the Upper House with 245 current members (including 12 nominees), requiring a minimum age of 30 years.
Money Bills (Article 110) hold exclusive jurisdiction in the Lok Sabha with limited advisory powers given to the Rajya Sabha.
Uttar Pradesh holds the maximum representation in Parliament with **80 Lok Sabha seats** and **31 Rajya Sabha seats**.
Joint sittings under Article 108 are summoned by the President and presided over by the Lok Sabha Speaker.
